name: Jebel Mebrah (Jabal Yibir), Tawiyean
area: Jebel Mebrah, also called Jabal Yibir or Jabal Mibrah, in the Hajar Mountains near the Al Tawiyean (Tuwiyain) area, on the Ras Al Khaimah and Fujairah border. Most sources place it in Ras Al Khaimah; Wikipedia puts the summit in Fujairah. The walk starts at a parking area near the top of the Mebrah mountain road, below a military installation.
gradeBasis: No government body or land operator publishes a grade for any walk on Jebel Mebrah. The grade is an editorial judgement from the walkers' write-ups found. The author of the loc.wiki trail pages (Patrick, of the non-commercial Patricks Hikes Facebook page) says the second half of the loop is suitable only for experienced hikers (loose rock, rough wadi ground, scrambling), that the exploration hike has many ascents and descents with no resting places and is fully exposed to the sun, and that readers should not try it without mountain experience, first aid, navigation and fitness. The start is high on a steep road (Wikipedia puts the police checkpoint at 1,227m), the area is remote, and access passes a military gate where entry is at the guards' discretion. Last checked October 2026.
distanceNote: Not confirmed. None of the three loc.wiki trail pages found (Patrick, Patricks Hikes) states a distance. The only distance in the one-way page is a point about 3km from the parking area where the track turns downhill toward the base of the summit. Peakvisor lists three unnamed computed routes of 17.0, 18.6 and 23.3 miles (about 27, 30 and 37km) but does not say where they start. Climbfinder gives 16.3km for the paved road climb, which is a cycling and driving climb, not the walk.
climbNote: Not confirmed for the walk. The loc.wiki pages give no ascent. Peakvisor lists 6,027 to 6,729 feet (about 1,837 to 2,051m) of total ascent for its three computed routes, but they appear to start far lower than the parking area and are not this walk. Climbfinder gives 1,432m of gain over 16.3km for the paved road climb to 1,504m. Elevation of the summit: 1,527m (Wikipedia, Peakvisor, SummitX/OpenStreetMap, 40thousandkm); 1,504m (Climbfinder); about 1,500m (Patrick); 1,350m (AskExplorer, for the end of the drivable road); 1,727m (MissionsOffroad, which looks like an error).

trailhead.name: Mebrah/Yibir parking area, near the top of the Jebel Mebrah road (Tawiyean side), below the military installation
trailhead.coordSource: Patrick (Patricks Hikes), loc.wiki trail pages 'Jebel Yibir Summit - One Way' and 'Jebel Yibir Summit Loop (Part exploration)' (both undated, listed near Tala, Ras Al Khaimah): parking spot 25.649070, 56.121293; a second trailhead for the upper trail at 25.650578, 56.123508. MissionsOffroad (published 2020, last modified 2024) gives other points: northern trail start 25.656696, 56.111661, southern trail start 25.625375, 56.124382, bottom checkpoint 25.606520, 56.125501 and top checkpoint 25.643800, 56.115270. Wikipedia gives the summit at 25.64833, 56.12917. The parking pin lies about 0.8km west of the Wikipedia summit coordinate.
trailhead.parking: Patrick describes a parking area at the top of the road, beyond a military gate where guards record the car and Emirates ID. Whether parking is permitted, how many cars it holds and whether it is open to the public is not confirmed. Wikipedia says visitors are usually allowed up to about 1,360m, roughly 1km before the military installations, after identification at the police checkpoint. Last checked October 2026.
trailhead.vehicle: Not confirmed. Patrick says the last 6km of the road is very steep and needs a strong car, and that the road was recently rebuilt and is in good condition. Wikipedia says the paved road from Al Tawiyean was completed in 2024 and has sections of 16% gradient. Reviewers on Wanderlog disagree: one says a sedan managed it and 4WD was not needed, another recommends 4WD for traction. AskExplorer reports many destroyed tyres at the corners.

routeDescription: Jebel Mebrah is a mountain in the Hajar range near Al Tawiyean. Its Arabic name is written جبل مبرح, and it is also called Jabal Yibir (جبل يبر). Wikipedia lists the spellings Jabal Al-Mebrah, Jabal Mibrah, Jabal Mebrah and Jebel Al Mebrah, and puts the summit between Fujairah and Ras Al Khaimah, in Fujairah. Peakvisor, Airial, Wanderlog and the loc.wiki trail pages place it in Ras Al Khaimah. The summit carries a military installation with radars and antennas, which Wikipedia says is not accessible to the public.

The route starts at a parking area near the top of the paved Mebrah mountain road, which climbs from the Al Tawiyean area. Patrick (Patricks Hikes) says a Ras Al Khaimah military gate sits on the way up; guards record the car and Emirates ID details, and entry is at their discretion. MissionsOffroad (2020, last modified 2024) describes a bottom checkpoint that is usually staffed at weekends and a top checkpoint with a boom barrier where entry can be refused. Photography at the top is not allowed and drones are banned (Patrick, Adventure Extreme page).

Patrick recorded a one-way walk from the parking area to the summit of what he calls the real Jebel Yibir, about 1,500m high. He took the lower of two parallel trails and heads toward Durdur village. Around the 3km point the track turns left and downhill to the base of the summit, then follows an unmarked connection onto rocky ground. The summit has three false summits, and the real one is the fourth high point, with a concrete foundation carrying a marker number. Views take in the Musandam mountains and Jebel Harf Tila. He suggests returning the same way.

Variants recorded by the same author: a loop that continues from the summit down to Wabsaqar village, then climbs to Durdur village on the plateau and returns to the cars, whose second half he rates for experienced hikers only (loose rock, rough wadi terrain, scrambling); a longer exploration hike, organised by Adventure Extreme in February, across several peaks and valleys past remote shepherd villages such as Kanan, which he calls an exploration and endurance hike with no resting places; and another track on a loc.wiki page 'Jebal Yabir', with views of the Dibba and Ras Al Khaimah coasts, a possible brief crossing into Oman and a Persian horned viper seen near the top. No source gives a distance for any of them.

There is no official trail, grade or waymarking. Patrick warns that GPS recordings may contain errors in wadi sections. The villages named are reached on foot; do not count on finding people or water in them. An Al Majalla essay (17 February 2024) describes people living in stone houses on the high peaks of Mibrah, who have refused offers to sell their land, so treat the area as lived-in private land and keep to tracks.
bestMonths: Not confirmed by any official source. Patrick's Adventure Extreme hike was in February (year not stated) and a commenter on the Jebal Yabir page calls it a winter hike. MissionsOffroad says the upper slopes are about 10 to 15 degrees Celsius cooler than the base, and often in cloud. Treat November to March as the sensible window.
startAdvice: Not confirmed by any official source. Patrick says the trail is fully exposed to the sun and advises at least 4 litres of water in February, more in other months. Start early, allow for the drive and the checkpoint, and leave time to get back down the steep road in daylight; reviewers on Wanderlog advise against driving it at night or in rain.
shade: None on the walk (Patrick: fully exposed; a commenter on the Jebal Yabir page also says no shade).
water: No water source is reported. Patrick advises at least 4 litres per person in February and more in other months. Carry all your own.
signal: Not confirmed. No source reports mobile signal on the walk. Download an offline map and track before you go.
fees: No fee for the walk or the road was found in any source opened. No entry charge is published by a government body. Last checked October 2026.
permits: No permit is published. Access depends on the military gate: guards record the vehicle and Emirates ID details and entry is at their discretion (Patrick, loc.wiki; MissionsOffroad). The summit area is a military installation and is not open to the public (Wikipedia, Patrick). Photography at the top is banned and drones are not allowed (Patrick). No source gives a rule for walking groups. Last checked October 2026.
hours: No opening hours found. MissionsOffroad says the bottom checkpoint is usually staffed at weekends and rarely on weekdays. Last checked October 2026.
closure: Current status cannot be confirmed. No government or land-operator page for Jebel Mebrah was found. Wikipedia says the paved road from Al Tawiyean was completed in 2024 and that visitors are usually let through to about 1,360m after identification. MissionsOffroad (published 2020, last modified 2024) says access was restricted after many accidents, that the road disappeared from Google Maps and that its status was unclear; it gives no dates or incident details. Patrick's pages are undated but describe the road as recently rebuilt and the gate as open at the guards' discretion. Last checked October 2026. Treat access as something the guards can refuse on the day.
safety: Access is not guaranteed. A military gate controls the road, guards record your car and Emirates ID, and they can refuse entry (Patrick; MissionsOffroad). The summit is a military installation and is off limits (Wikipedia).

There is no official trail, grade or waymarks. Patrick says the loop is for experienced hikers only and warns his GPS tracks may be wrong in wadi sections. Go with a licensed guide if you have not walked it before.
Heat and exposure: the walk is fully in the sun (Patrick). Do not walk in summer. Carry at least 4 litres of water per person, more in warm months.

No news report, police notice or rescue naming Jebel Mebrah was found in English or Arabic searches in October 2026. That is not evidence that it is safe. MissionsOffroad says the road saw many accidents but gives no details, and AskExplorer reports many destroyed tyres at the corners.

The steep road is part of the risk. Wikipedia reports 16% sections and Dangerous Roads reports up to 18%. Reviewers advise checking tyres and engine temperature, driving slowly and not driving it in rain or at night.

Flash floods: the descent to Wabsaqar and other wadi sections lie on wadi ground, and the mountain drains into the Wadi Tawiyean and Wadi Naqab basins (Wikipedia). No source gives a flood rule for this route. Do not start in or after rain.
Persian horned vipers were reported near the top on a nearby Patrick track. Do not put hands in crevices.

Tell someone your route and return time, hike with a companion, and turn back early. Allow for the drive down; there are no restaurants, washrooms, fuel stations or huts after Tawiyean (Wanderlog reviewers).
carry: At least 4 litres of water per person (Patrick, for February; more in other months)
Offline map and GPS track, with a spare power bank
Sturdy hiking boots with good grip
Emirates ID or passport and the vehicle registration for the gate
Warm layer for early starts and cloud on the upper slopes
Rubbish bag to take everything out (Patrick)
emergency: Police 999 (Ras Al Khaimah Police, as listed on visitjebeljais.com/jais-hiking); ambulance 998 and civil defence 997 (Ajman government emergency numbers page, ajman.ae). Last checked October 2026.
driveNote: Not confirmed. No source opened gave a drive time to Al Tawiyean or to the top of the road from Ras Al Khaimah city, Dubai or Abu Dhabi. The road starts in the Al Tawiyean area (Wikipedia; Patrick). Climbfinder lists the paved climb as 16.3km with 1,432m of gain, but does not label its start point. Wanderlog reviewers say there are no facilities after Tawiyean.
intro: Jebel Mebrah, also called Jabal Yibir, is a Hajar mountain near Al Tawiyean with a paved road to a military gate near the top. The walks recorded there are unofficial, have no grade, distance or waymarks in any government source, and start only if the guards let you through. It is a route for experienced hikers in the cooler months.

_doubts: WHICH PLACE IS THIS: reasonably confident, not fully. 'Mebrah' and 'Yibir' are two names for the same mountain (Wikipedia Jebel Al Mebrah, Peakvisor, Dangerous Roads, AskExplorer, loc.wiki 'Mebrah/Yibir'). Spellings searched: Jebel Mebrah, Jabal Mebrah, Jebel Al Mebrah, Jabal Mibrah, Jebel Yibir, Jabal Yibir, Jabal al Mebrah, Jebel Mibrah, جبل مبرح. No Arabic news page naming it was found.

EMIRATE: Wikipedia says the summit is in Fujairah (citing the Fujairah government portal) and that the mountain is between Fujairah and Ras Al Khaimah. Peakvisor, Wanderlog, Airial, Apple Maps (search title) and the loc.wiki pages say Ras Al Khaimah; AskExplorer says Fujairah; mountain-forecast.com says Oman (clearly wrong). The page says Ras Al Khaimah as asked by the brief. If the summit and the walking ground are in Fujairah, this guide may belong under Fujairah and a different authority may apply.

NO OFFICIAL ROUTE: no government body, Visit Ras Al Khaimah, Visit Jebel Jais or Fujairah Adventures page for a Mebrah walk was found. Everything about the walk rests on three or four trail pages by one author (Patrick, Patricks Hikes, via loc.wiki, undated, a non-commercial Facebook page and Wikiloc content). The author, and the loc.wiki domain's relationship to Wikiloc, should be checked by a fact-checker; Wikiloc and AllTrails pages could not be opened.

DISTANCE, CLIMB AND TIME: none found for the walk. Peakvisor's three computed routes (about 27 to 37km, 1,837 to 2,051m ascent, 8h45 to 11h) have no stated start and look like they start low on the mountain; not used. Climbfinder's 16.3km and 1,432m is the paved road climb. Not confirmed on the page.

SUMMIT HEIGHT: 1,527m (Wikipedia, Peakvisor, OSM via SummitX, 40thousandkm, Dangerous Roads), 1,504m (Climbfinder), about 1,500m (Patrick), 1,350m (AskExplorer, end of drivable road), 1,727m (MissionsOffroad, which also calls it the UAE's highest, which conflicts with Wikipedia saying Jebel Jais's summit is in Oman and a point at 1,892m is the UAE's highest). The MissionsOffroad figure is not used. Wikipedia prominence 216m vs Peakvisor 248m or about 210m.

WHICH SUMMIT: Patrick calls the point he reaches the real Jebel Yibir, about 1,500m, with a concrete foundation and marker number, and the Wikipedia summit coordinate (25.64833, 56.12917) carries the military installation. Whether his summit and the military top are the same, or whether the walk stays outside the military boundary, is not confirmed. Do not imply walkers may enter the installation.

TRAILHEAD: the parking pin comes from one author. It lies about 0.8km west of the Wikipedia summit coordinate and about 1km from MissionsOffroad's top checkpoint (25.6438, 56.11527); the Wikipedia text puts the usual limit for visitors about 1km before the military installation, so these are broadly consistent, but the pin could not be checked on a map and may be inside or beyond the restricted zone at times. OpenStreetMap could not be queried.

ACCESS RULES: all information on the gate is from Patrick, MissionsOffroad (2020, modified 2024), Wikipedia and Wanderlog reviewers. No police or military source. Whether civilians may park and walk at all, whether a pass is needed, and on which days the gate is staffed are not confirmed. MissionsOffroad says access was restricted after many accidents and that the road vanished from Google Maps; Wikipedia and Patrick describe the road as open and recently rebuilt. These may be different dates.

ROAD WORKS AND DATE OF THE ROAD: Wikipedia says the road was completed in 2024. Peakvisor and OSM were updated in 2024. Patrick's pages are undated and describe a recently rebuilt road. Current condition not checked.

INCIDENTS: English and Arabic searches (rescue, accident, إنقاذ, شرطة رأس الخيمة, طريق جبل مبرح) returned no report naming Jebel Mebrah, Jabal Yibir or Mibrah. Reports found were for other places (Wadi Shahah, 15 July 2026; Wadi Huqail, 14 November 2024; Wadi Naqab rescues per Wikipedia). The search tool is weak on Arabic local news, so absence of reports is not proof. 'Many accidents' (MissionsOffroad) is unsourced and undated.

FLASH FLOODS AND CLOSURES: no flood rule or closure notice for this route was found. The flood bullet is general wadi advice, not a quoted rule. The Wikipedia drainage statement (divide between the Wadi Tawiyean and Wadi Naqab basins) is the only hydrology source.

VEHICLE: Patrick says a strong car, Wanderlog reviewers split between sedan and 4WD, AskExplorer reports 'relatively quick and easy drive' with narrow switchbacks and many destroyed tyres. Left as not confirmed.

GRADE: Difficult is my editorial reading of Patrick's comments plus the remoteness and the access, not a published grade. Patrick gives no formal rating. The easy option may be a short walk near the parking area; I found no source describing one.
SEASON: months scores are editorial (Patrick's February hike, a 'winter hike' comment, and MissionsOffroad's 10 to 15 degrees cooler claim). No official season given.

VILLAGES AND LAND: Durdur, Wabsaqar and Kanan are named by Patrick; Al Majalla (17 February 2024) describes people living on Mibrah's high peaks and refusing to sell land. Whether the villages are inhabited today, and whether the paths cross private land, is not confirmed.

OMAN BORDER: the Jebal Yabir page says the route may briefly enter Oman. The Mebrah summit is close to the Musandam border (Peakvisor: parent peak Jebel Qihwi in Oman). Do not cross the border; no source gives the line.

PHOTO: only one Commons file was fully checked before the Commons API rate-limited the session: 'Start of the road leading from Al Tuwiyain towards Jabal Yibir.jpg', by IbrahimKumar, CC BY-SA 4.0, taken 10 December 2024, in Category Jabal Al-Mebrah, camera coordinate 25.562306, 56.078554, which is about 11km in a straight line from the walk start, at the bottom of the access road. Other candidates in the category (Jabal Yibir - 1 to 10, Jebel Yibir - At the top - Ras Al Khaimah.jpg, View of Jabal Yibir -1.jpg) were found by title only; author, licence and location were not checked. A fact-checker may prefer one of those.
NO DRIVE TIME found from Ras Al Khaimah, Dubai or Abu Dhabi; omitted.

page.status: Unmarked route: there is no official trail, waymarks or grade. Access is through a military gate at the guards' discretion. Go with a licensed guide if you have not walked it before.
page.gradeBasis: No government body or operator grades this route. Difficult is an editorial judgement: a walkers' write-up rates the loop for experienced hikers only, it is fully in the sun and remote, and access passes a military gate.
route: Drive up the paved Mebrah road from the Al Tawiyean area to a parking area near the top. A military gate sits on the way, where guards record your car and Emirates ID. Entry is at their discretion. The summit itself is a military installation and is closed to the public.

One walker (Patrick, Patricks Hikes) recorded a walk from the parking area towards Durdur village, then a left turn downhill after about 3km to the base of the summit. An unmarked link leads onto rocky ground. There are three false summits and the fourth high point has a concrete foundation with a marker number. He suggests returning the same way.

The same author recorded a loop that drops to Wabsaqar village and climbs to Durdur village on the plateau, and a longer hike past shepherd villages such as Kanan. He rates the loop for experienced hikers only. No source gives a distance for any of them.
